utterances.text: I'm sorry. My colleague is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting my learned friend. But regarding the admittance of the evidence P00610 in relation to Prilep, I would like to say, in page 10019, the Prosecutor says, upon suggestion that the Prosecutor claims that so-called national joint enterprise exists, it is not just incorrect but it is also inflammatory. This is all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. While we are distracted, the technical operators assure me that the change in sound that occurred during the playing of that was on the recording itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Carry on, please, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the record, Your Honour, at no time has the Prosecution accused that the nation of Macedonia being part of a joint criminal enterprise, and nor did I do so today, on page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, just so that the record is clear, going back to your last response, Dr. Markovski, you did tell us earlier in your testimony that, when you spoke to the media as the official spokesperson of the army, you were giving the official position of the army and the Ministry of Defence. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official positions of the defence; that is to say, to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this video-clip, please, and its transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P00611. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like for our learned friend to explain whether it is admitted and received as in evidence just the portion we viewed or the entire video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if necessary, we can finish watching the rest of the clip. I believe it is only perhaps a short -- a short period of time. It was my intention to submit -- to submit the entire video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber's understanding is that the whole clip has been tendered and is an exhibit, Ms. Residovic. Please continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Moving on to another topic, Dr. Markovski, after the crisis ended, or after the Ohrid Agreement was signed on the 13th of August, 2001, there was a first process of disarmament, which occurred during August and September 2001, and that was called Operation Essential Harvest. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Macedonian language, it is called Essential Harvest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And during that activity or operation, Essential Harvest, I believe, according to your own report, 3.875 weapons were collected from the so-called NLA, which exceeded the figure of 3.000 weapons which was the amount agreed upon during negotiations between NATO and the NLA. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This data was received from the NATO structures, and they were the implementing party of this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Then there was also a second disarmament process, if I'm correct, which occurred between the 1st of November and the 15th of December, 2003. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is correct, and I already envisaged what you're going to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, first of all, this second disarmament process was organised by the government of the Republic of Macedonia, which encouraged the voluntary surrender of illegal weapons by members of the population. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I was the commander of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And more than 7.000 weapons of various kinds were collected during this second disarmament process in 2003. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for your precision. Turning to another topic, at page 10632 of the transcript, you told my learned colleague that the activities of the NLA were not supported in the official statements of the ethnic Albanian political parties. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is corroborated by several examples in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Dr. Markovski, are you familiar with the so-called Prizren Agreement that was signed by Arben Xhaferi, president of the DPA party; Imer Imeri, president of the PDP party; and Ali Ahmeti, as the political representative of the NLA on the 22nd of May, 2001? Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, that document, it is actually titled: "The declaration of the Albanian leaders in Macedonia regarding the reforming and peace process in the Republic of Macedonia." And, in that document, three leaders, the two leaders of the political parties and Mr. Ali Ahmeti, agreed on a common action. Doesn't that illustrate, Dr. Markovski, some official support for the NLA from the leaders of the ethnic Albanian political parties?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, you are well-informed that this Prizren Agreement, its purpose was to provide greater rights for the Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia; that is to say, to regulate the rights of the Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia. This is a problem that started in 1990, with Geert Arhens, as a facilitator for the former Yugoslavia. It was terminated later on. I'm very glad that these two political entities, DPA and PDP, overcame their prejudice and they accepted, together with the representative - probably I will remember his name - Peter Feith, in his presence, to negotiate and discuss these issues in Prizren. The Ohrid Framework Agreement does not extend the rights of the Albanians. The Ohrid Framework Agreement re-regulates the Macedonian society; and on the basis of the agreement achieved by the four most relevant political parties in the Republic of Macedonia, these rights do not apply just to the Albanians but all the other ethnic communities in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. But my question was actually a little bit different. My question was simply this: Didn't the so-called Prizren Agreement, signed by Ali Ahmeti and leaders of two -- the two main ethnic Albanian political parties, doesn't the Prizren Agreement illustrate some official support for the NLA from the leaders of the leading ethnic Albanian parties?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In no sense, it does not support the armed violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But it would support other aspects of the -- let me put my question hopefully a little bit more clearly. It would lend some support to the political goals of the NLA, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These political goals of the NLA are not political goals of the NLA. Like I told you back in 1992, Macedonia started with this process. It was terminated in 1995. And with the Ohrid Framework Agreement as a political agreement, all these issues received their confirmation. So it is not like you said, and we are not discussing any support by the DPA and PDP of any kind of conditions that were given in order to provide for expanded rights of any of the ethnic communities in Macedonia, especially not to provide this through armed violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Now, Dr. Markovski, I'm required by the rules to put some propositions to you; and if you can, I'd like to you answer yes or no. If you need to expand, obviously, you can do that. I'd like to put to you, Dr. Markovski, that the situation in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001 amounted to an internal armed conflict between the NLA and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult precisely and clear, in the focus of a black and white, to be able to define such a situation. In my opinion, and according to the research I conducted, and it has been verified on a scientific level by the academy for sciences in Bulgaria as well, my position has been admitted as a scientific contribution, regarding the definition on crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, both according to the factual situation and the relevant legal determinations. There was a crisis and it was terminated before its escalation, before it grew into an internal armed conflict, of course, with full support coming from the international factor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's true, isn't it, Dr. Markovski, that the NLA was an organised armed force, with a military structure and a functioning chain of command?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, Dr. Markovski, that the members of the NLA wore uniforms and observed the laws and customs of war?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two aspects in your questions. Sometimes they wore uniforms; sometimes they didn't. They wore them in certain situations; and, quite often, they would change their clothes, becoming ordinary citizens. The second aspect of your question, I apologise, I forgot what it was. Can you please remind me of the second part of the question. It seems that I am already tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's my fault. I should have asked you a simpler question. It's true, isn't it, that the NLA --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that the NLA observed the laws and customs of war?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely they did not observe. I don't want to remind you again about the displacement, the putting fires, the terrorist activities, abuse of civilian population, forcing the civilian Albanian population to provide support, et cetera. These are not the rules of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, it's true, isn't it, that between February and August 2001, the NLA and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia engaged in offensive and defensive military actions on numerous occasions.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not so. The armed Albanian extremist structures, there were situations where they would be engaged in armed provocations and incidents, and the security structures of the Republic of Macedonia did not engage in fighting, with the exception of the five to six incidents that we mentioned as organised actions ordered by the president. In all other situations, they were present in order to demonstrate force; that is to say, to prevent any person or group that is trying to act contrary to the legal provisions in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Dr. Markovski, that between February and August 2001, the NLA took control of large amounts of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely did not have control. It was present in certain populated areas, and it was hiding behind the citizens. They did not establish their local control, because, in the crisis regions, the mayors or the leaders of the municipality, they operated with all their authority, both in Lipkovo, in Tetovo, or any other of the crisis regions. There is not a single example where the head of the local self-government was not able to perform his or her duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Dr. Markovski, that, in 2001, the NLA military activities were carried out to further the political objectives of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the political objectives of the NLA; political goals of their leaders, I would say. And this is more than obvious even today. Unfortunately, the people who bled remain without any rights. The few of those that we saw in the squares yesterday, now they sit in comfortable cabinets with rather good salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, Dr. Markovski, that the Ohrid Framework Agreement, signed on the 13th of August, 2001, to a large degree, formalised the political objectives of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political objectives of the NLA were to seize territory in order to be able to have control over these territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So is your answer to my question a yes or a no?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. It's true isn't it, Dr. Markovski, that between the 10th and 12th of August, 2001, Major Mitre Despodov never received a direct order from the president, Boris Trajkovski. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that Major Mitre Despodov received an order from the president. Yesterday, I offered another piece of evidence, and this is the report of the commander of the 1st Guardist Brigade dated 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the record, I believe the witness is referring to Exhibit P00304.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's true, Dr. Markovski, that the actions of the police forces in and around Ljuboten, on 12 August, were not legitimate and amounted to violations of the laws and customs of war. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is very complex in order to provide a simple answer. They were legitimate; and, in Ljuboten, there were legitimate targets on which one should have had and did act. Ljuboten was a serious threat for the security of the capital city in Macedonia because of the possibility to create additional tensions in this region with a possibility for a link up along the line of Kumanovo, Skopje, and Radusa; and, on the other hand, a great danger, if one does not react on time, for certain terrorist groups to be infiltrated in the capital city of the Republic of Macedonia, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, isn't it true that are you biased in your perspective towards the events in Republic of Macedonia in 2001 and, therefore, you cannot accept that the NLA was an organised armed force?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, I am not biased, and I don't have any prejudice. At present, I also deal with issues related to security. I am member of the Balkan Forum for Security, an NGO for defence issues, and we also have members of the Albanian ethnic origin and also one member of the DUI political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And because of that same bias, Dr. Markovski, you cannot accept that the situation in Macedonia during 2001 was an internal armed conflict, can you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Markovski, for your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Markovski, I will have several more questions to ask regarding the cross-examination by my learned colleague from the OTP? A while ago, you mentioned that you feel tired. Can we continue or maybe I can suggest a break and maybe continue afterwards and then work in a single session.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there such a probability, I would be more than grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That could only occur if you lost some of your time at the end, Mr. Apostolski, because we can't afford two breaks between now and 1.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought it would be convenient to take a break now, 20 to 25 minutes; and, afterwards, we will have enough time until 1345 to work in a single session, at least according to go my calculations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, but that would require the witness to go through a full session. That, you would prefer?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you will be more ready. Very well. We will adjourn, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, do you remember that yesterday my colleague, the Prosecutor, asked you several questions related to certain provisions of the old and the new Law on Defence? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The attorney to Mr. Boskoski, my colleague Edina Residovic, asked you similar questions two days ago. Do you recall that as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that we discussed this issue as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On page 10658 of the transcript, answering the questions of my colleague, Ms. Residovic, you stated that the president of the state was the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember, and I confirm it. This is pursuant to Article 79 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, on page 10675 of the transcript, you stated that also, when performing the office of the Supreme Commander, the president of the Republic has no restrictions. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this, and I mentioned it today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also stated that the president was the Supreme Commander of the armed forces in both times of war and peace. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how the constitution provides it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When a state of war is not declared, would any regulation prevent the president from issuing an order to both the army and the police performing the authentic competencies vested in him by the constitution?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitution does not limit the president's competencies of being the Supreme Commander to either the situation of war or peace. He is a Supreme Commander at all times, and there are no restrictions in this sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My learned friend, the Prosecutor, asked you several questions relating to the General Staff of the army. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was the position of my learned colleague that the new law only formalised this situation actually existing, that a General Staff actually existed with all its functions?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it, and I did harass the esteemed Mr. Saxon a bit because I was not clear about this formulation. Probably, is it is customary for you, the lawyers, but we military officers use it very rarely. Now I became clear what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know what organisation and formation of the army is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what it prescribes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ministries, as bodies of the state administration, have the systemization. What is a systemization for the ministries for the Serbian [as interpreted] army is the organisation and the formation. It prescribes the specific and the complete organisation and structure of the army, starting from the General Staff, until the last unit, at the lowest level, and prescribes also the obligations and the duties for all those levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me who is issuing the order on organisation and formation?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not an order. It is called -- the title is: Organisation and formation of the army. It is it not an order. The title of the document is: Organisation and formation. This is a document passed by the president, by the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, in line 17, on page 58, "Serbian army" is mentioned and it should be "Macedonian army."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no intention of mentioning the Serbian army. Maybe I said it, but it obviously applies to the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look again at the Exhibit P606, item 1. That is the Law on Defence on 1992, and let's focus on Article 15 of the law. Could we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Article 15, competences of the president, in execution of the defence of the Republic. Item 4 says: "Prescribes organisation and formation of the army." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And has he prescribed this? I'm referring here to the president.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An army could not exist if there is no prescribed organisation and formation of the army. So the first organisation and formation of the army is prescribed within the army of the Republic of Macedonia was established, in 1992; and further on, any transformation or restructuring of the army would presuppose a new organisation and formation. The army of the Republic of Macedonia underwent more than five transformation restructuring; so when each of those occurred, a new systemization and organisation was prescribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it also regulate the composition and the competencies of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I said what organisation and formation presupposes, I confirmed this, and I confirm it again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In line 61, "organisation and formation," rather than "systemization and organisation."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall and do you know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please. Microphone for the counsel please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could you put on your microphone, please, counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I inadvertently switched the microphone off or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who was the first chief of the General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I know. At that time, General Major Mitre Arsovski was appointed, and later he was promoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown - the expert, I apologise - 1D1324. This is a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the upper left corner, we read president of the Republic of Macedonia, the date is the 16th of March, 1992, and confidential number 53. We have here decree number 1 of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, dated 16th March 1992. In the upper right-hand corner, we have the seal of the ministry for national defence; and below it, it reads: "Pursuant to Article 15, paragraph 1, item 16 of the Law on Defence of the Republic of Macedonia, Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia number 8/92, appointed to peacetime and wartime formation are, number 1, General Major Arsovski Milan Mitre, born on November 1st, 1936, in the Ministry of Defence for Republic of Macedonia for chief of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Do you see this in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And it is signed by the president, Kiro Gligorov. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wish to make a brief comment. The army of the Republic of Macedonia actually started functioning from March 1992; and as far as I can see, this is the first decree. This is one of the types of documents that the president and the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia can issue or sign. What we have here is his first decree, the decree of the then-president, Kiro Gligorov, appointing as chief of General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia, General Major, Mr. Arsovski Milan Mitre.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 2D00104. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what is the difference between the new and the old Law on Defence with regards to the competences of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel that we discussed this several times already, and I stated that the main aim of the new law was to follow the need of transformation of the system, defence system. In that sense, specifically, answering this question you asked me, until this time, we had a situation where many of the by-laws were signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia alone. Many by-laws, secondary legislation items were created, while the new law has dealt with many of the issues. I'm not saying that it dealt with all of the issues, but it dealt, itself, the law dealt with the many of the issues that were previously regulated by by-laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there, at any moment, a gap or vacuum in the legal position of the General Staff or of other bodies of army?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Then the army couldn't function, which was not the case with the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it agree with your knowledge and any study of documents, has the prime minister ever issued an order to the police with regards to a combat action in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never found any documents speaking to what you just said. I have never seen anything of the sort. But also from my practical experience, because I was a witness to many events, I know with certainty and I can confirm that in no situation has the prime minister issued any order to the police in this sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I thank you for the answers, and I will move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. Apostolski, I don't believe we have in evidence the organisation and structure of the army as it existed in 2001, before the new Law on Defence came into existence, is that correct, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that was the point of my questioning, that we don't have them at the moment but they existed and do exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for what it's worth, I believe this may be partly addressed in what is Exhibit P00321, which is known as the Macedonian briefing pack. But I see my colleague Ms. Residovic is shaking her head, so I may be wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point I make - thank you, Mr. Saxon - I think I really should address to you, Mr. Apostolski, and that is, if this document is relied upon, we will need to have it in the form that it existed at the time directly relevant to this indictment. Can we ask you to provide that?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will make our best efforts, Your Honours, to provide the Chamber with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure your best efforts will be more than successful. Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could the witness please be shown -- Dr. Markovski please be shown the Exhibit 1D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Until the document is displayed, do you remember that the Prosecutor has shown you this document and that you discussed it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You discussed, on page 10750 of the transcript, and the Prosecutor asserted that, nowhere in the text, he sees that those were preventative measures for the defence of the city of Skopje, and that this order has been issued since there was a clear and present danger. Could you please look at the upper paragraph, in the Macedonian version, starting with the words: "On the basis of Article 76, paragraph 2."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, 79, paragraph 2. Could you please read it until the end of it. Tell me, it mentions here some measures, "timely measures."

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we have here is the establishment of the command for the defence of the city of Skopje. This is a decision to establish this command, and it reads: "Pursuant to Article 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia, and Article 18, items 4 and 5 of the Law on Defence of the Republic of Macedonia, and in order to undertake timely measures for the defence of the city Skopje, I hereby bring the following ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you please explain to me what "timely measures" would mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Timely measures would mean that, on the basis of some assessments and reviews, prevention measures need to be passed, in terms of preventing something under desirable from happening or in order to deter something undesirable. So this relates to prevention.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you remember the question related to the infiltration of the so-called NLA in Skopje - that is on page 10748 and 10749 of the transcript - and the entry of the so-called NLA into Aracinovo? The Prosecutor suggested that that was an imminent danger to Skopje and it has occupied Aracinovo and Vaksince. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, first, whether the so-called NLA has occupied any settlement? I'm now referring to a village or a city. Has it done this through any combat action?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found such document; but knowing the situation, there was nothing of the sort there. I wish to clarify something. Probably, we have mentioned this term "seizing or occupying" very often. But in the science, I don't what it is like in the law, and I make a disclaimer because I'm insufficiently proficient in the law, but to seize or occupy something means to establish power, government. That would mean that institutions of the government in that location would be unable to function. This is the aspect from which I wanted to explain this term, "seizing or occupying."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And I will ask you now about Aracinovo, specifically. In which way has the so-called NLA seized Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aracinovo, we will go back to the notion of seizing or occupying, but they actually entered Aracinovo through infiltration.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What does infiltration mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means furtively, probably or not probably, but surely, because, otherwise, they would have been observed, and they have also brought weapons in. When these groups infiltrated, there was a group of 250 to 260 arm the extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And around Aracinovo, were any security forces there?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the entry to Aracinovo from Skopje and at the exit towards Nikustak, there were check-points of the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that they entered the village of Aracinovo without fight?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This means without fight, illegally.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness and counsel to slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know whether the so-called NLA established its power in Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a period of some ten days, and we had a situation when the citizens, the inhabitants of Aracinovo, started leaving the village, fearing from the infiltrated armed extremist groups; but in Aracinovo, these groups have not established power or government.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean, have I understood you well, that there were security forces around Aracinovo, but still those groups managed to infiltrate the village of Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said. Actually, this is what I meant. I don't know whether I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did they manage to establish their mayor in Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The same mayor remained, before that, during that, and after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Today, you marked certain locations that were under the control of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to correct you as well. They were not under the NLA control. They were villages where there were armed extremists present.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In those villages that you marked - for the transcript, I indicate this is Exhibit P00608 - were there fighting between the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Today, you marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P00608.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You marked several locations that were indicated to you. Could you tell me, how were throws locations, and I would say in parenthesis, "seized" by the armed groups?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same way, without fighting. There is no seizing, with or without parenthesis; there was only presence of armed extremists in these locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was their power established in these locations, settlements?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The mayors of these settlements remained in office and operated carrying out all the competences.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In relation to this exhibit, I have one further question. The Prosecutor has asked you to connect them, connect these settlements with lines.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wondering why. I did not understand the purpose of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there, in your opinion, because you have been a witness to those events in 2001, for instance, the item 1, near Celopek, is linked with Jegunovce, would there be movements free movements of so-called NLA between those two locations, from one extreme of the line to the other?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I told this to the Prosecutor as well. They could only move illegally here disguised as civilians or in some other way. I don't know. But there were no free movements between these two points. There was no free movement in terms that they would have been able to move freely and openly carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel and the witness to slow down for us and for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You mentioned "illegally." What would this mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Illegally would mean furtively, in a clandestine fashion, camouflaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For the transcript, were they moving from one point to the other wearing uniforms? Were they able to do so?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could do this during one point in time, today or tomorrow, but not during the entire period in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You spoke about the operations, for instance, in Vaksince. Let me ask you how much time it took for armed forces to reclaim the control of Vaksince?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the action of the security forces lasted a day and a half or possibly a maximum of two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know how many casualty were there on the side the security forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single casualty.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the largest operation of the security forces around Tetovo in March 2001, were there any casualties on the side of the security forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the period 23rd and 24th of March when this took place, no, not a single casualty.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How many days did the operation last?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, around two and a half days. Actually, it started on one day and then it was continued, so it lasted around two and a half days.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. I will move to another topic now, Mr. Markovski. Do you remember, yesterday, page 10822, my learned colleague from the OTP was asking you where from you draw your conclusion, in paragraph 208 in your report, that the president directly by phone issued an order to Major Despodov in order to perform certain tasks in relation to Ljuboten? You were shown the footnote in the report by Ljupco Kostandinov. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When preparing your expert report, did you have access to the statements given by other witnesses in this case and statements given by witnesses to the investigators from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I used several documents; and why I chose precisely this one as a corroboration of my position, I really cannot say. But yesterday, and today again, I referred to one more document that specifically discusses this issue. Probably, I thought these documents, at least not all of them, were that important in order to be presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P304, please; page 2, if it can be opened, please. I apologise. Can we have page number 1 back, please. Let's wait for the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you review this document also, because there is a document you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document. This is the report about the situation in the area of the 3rd Guardist Brigade prepared by the brigade, and they report to their superior, General Sokol Mitrevski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, one can read: "The action, which was to remain secret and upon order by the president, was supposed to begin on the 11th of August, 2001, at 0430 hours ..." Does this correspond with your conclusion given in paragraph 208?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what it reads, and that is why I referred to the corroboration of my positions that I present in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, I'm going to read a portion of the testimony by Major Despodov given before the Trial Chamber. On the page 2580, lines 5, 6, and 7, Major Mitre Despodov says the following: "I received instructions from the president that I have to undertake measures and activities that are under my competency." Is there testimony in accordance with your report?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is with my report and also in accordance with the documents that I have cited in corroboration to the claims in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Dr. Markovski please be shown 65 ter 2D296, page 2D02-1950, and if we can focus on paragraph 38, please. This is the statement given by Colonel Blazo Kopacev, given to the investigators from the ICTY, and I'm going to read it out loud because it is an English version. I'm going to read it in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 38, somewhere in the middle, it says: "I emphasise that the only source of my knowledge about the alleged order by the president to the Major Despodov, for the action which he allegedly received by phone from the president directly, is Major Despodov himself." Does this statement, by Colonel Kopacev, is in accordance with your report, to be more precise, paragraph 208?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Going further, do you remember today the Prosecutor has shown to you a video-clip with a statement given by Vlado Buckovski - this is Exhibit P611 - with respect to the incident in Karpalak?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown what is 65 ter 1D856. This is page 4, paragraph 21. This is the statement given by Mr. Vlado Buckovski, provided to the ICTY investigators in relation to the event in Karpalak.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And it reads the following: [In English] "Humiliation after Karpalak attack. Even president's advisors advised him to signing of the Ohrid Agreement should coincide in time with some sort of military victory. Ljubotenski Bacila was a convenient occasion to demonstrate force." [Interpretation] Does this statement also points to the fact that the president was also advised for some action in Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was both advised. And if you can -- if you followed my responses to the Prosecutor today, when we were commenting on one of my position, I already mentioned that he was under pressure, not just advised, but also under pressure for the need for doing something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers, Dr. Markovski. Now let me move to another topic. Is it true that, during a war or an armed conflict, the rules of military law are being applied.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. This is why they exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And if these are applied to the participants of the armed conflict, they are allowed to perform certain activities or to perform activities in certain specific manner?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Previously, we were talking that, during a war or an armed conflict, the rules of laws of war are being applied, and these -- those are applied to the participants, they are you allowed to conduct concern activities or perform them in a certain manner?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who is supposed to allow them or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In this specific case, if there was an armed conflict, it would be allowed for the members of the parties to the armed conflict to kill the members of the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is far from the interpretation of any rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember you have been asked by the Prosecution about the structure and the functioning of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And do you remember that you pointed out that, according to your opinion, the NLA was not organised in the same manner as an army or party to the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is what I would claim right now, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D256, Exhibit 1D256, page number 14; ERN 1D00-6449. Can we please scroll down, under the title: Conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read it out loud. The document originates from and this is the report from the international crisis group, dated 5th of April, 2001. This is the portion that you can see in front of you in the screen. And the first part, under the conclusion, it reads as follows: "The series of incidents in Tanusevci spiralled out of control, setting in motion a series of unplanned actions by loosely coordinated guerilla cells. The shooting from the hills above Tetovo does not appear to have been part of a larger strategic plan, but rather an improvised show of strength to test government resolve and radicalise ethnic Albanian opinion." Does the content of this document would agree and coincide with your professional and personal opinion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this is well-known document to me. I don't know why you don't have it in the Macedonian version. I do have it in my records because I work on analytical analysis, and this paragraph coincides with my position presented here, and on the other hand, I have a great admiration and respect for this institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D260, the page would be 1D00-7798. This is an article from Jane's Defence Weekly, Sunday, 29 August 2001, and the text IS titled: How many weapons in Macedonia, in the lower part of this document. Somewhere, in the middle of the text, IS the paragraph starting with the wording: "NATO." Can we scroll to the lower part of the page, please, the paragraph starting with: "NATO must deal with the fact that the NLA does not have a fully integrated chain of command, nor centralised logistics. Even NLA leaders are unlikely to have reliable figures for weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, does the contents of this document, if accepted, would coincide with your professional and expert opinion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also write in the report that according to the international factor; that is, the people who somehow are not directly linked are not under the influence of the events in the Republic of Macedonia, and this is why I would believe that they have a more realistic view on the events that were going on in 2001. According to their data, the armed groups, the total number would be around 2800. However, in order to maintain a realistic view in my report, I also dealt with the number of 5.000, together with the people who provided logistic support, provided by some of the members of the armed extremist group back in 2001, and this was corroborated by their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 5485 [as interpreted], page 1D009148. The exhibit is P485. Let me move to another document. It seems it was a mistake in my records. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 1D1044, the page 1D00-8570.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This document comes from the Department Of Defence of the US government, and this is about June 2001. Item number 2 reads as follows: "The infrastructure of the NLA is designed and best suited for independent guerilla tactics, a lose organisational structure, low interdependency on other NLA groups and commanders. Individual commanders have authority to establish new fighting groups and to evolve fighter structure to meet the military requirement. "NLA brigades have similar structure to UCK structure. NLA fighters are divided into independent operational zones. Local commander have decision-making authority. Individual commanders have autonomy in planning of attacks within their operational zones." Dr. Markovski, does the content of this document, if accepted, would coincide with your professional and expert opinion?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this is a -- a document from the US government that has a disclaimer at the top of it, saying: "Warning. This is an information report, not finally evaluated intelligence." We don't know who produced the document or the source of the information, and the Chamber has held, I think on at least two occasions now, that without -- with this kind of disclaimer and without more accurate information regarding the source, such a document should not be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the expert confirmed the content of this document; and, number two, this is a credible document from the Department Of Defence of the US government. This Trial Chamber already admitted some other evidence coming from relevant organisation without knowing the precise source. However, it was admitted into evidence; for instance, the NATO package material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Documents of this particular type the Chamber has not admitted, and that will be our position on this one, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would like to move to another question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall, yesterday, you were shown a video-clip in relation to Radusa, and the activity of helicopters was depicted and a flying aeroplane. You confirmed that these are aircrafts that belong to the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were very precise saying that the aeroplane did not engage?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I confirm this assertion again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please, then, tell me what was the plane doing at that time at that particular location?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a confirmation, we are discussing two planes, not just one, during this period above Radusa, and I confirmed this by saying that the basic rule in engaging both planes and helicopters is that, when they are assigned to a mission, they undergo certain preparations. Usually, these missions can be combat missions or reconnaissance missions. In this case, the case of the two planes -- or, I apologise, they can be both reconnaissance and combat missions. And if these two planes had a combat mission or operation, they would have been armed with rockets. Additionally, the basic rule would be that an aeroplane or helicopter which goes into a combat operation cannot return with the same rockets. In this case, since there was no activities, the planes did not engage, there could have been no combat above Radusa, but exclusively a reconnaissance one. So, if there was combat mission, they would have used their rockets. As a corroboration of this, I will tell you something else that came to my mind. During the NATO campaign on our northern neighbour, when the aviation was to the capable of locating its targets, they would always shoot and use their rockets in areas where they would not cause any damage or a threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this additional clarification in this regard. Let me move to another topic now. Do you recall, Dr. Markovski, that you were asked by the Prosecutor about planning of operations?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Allow me to ask you the following: Would terrorists plan their own activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the level that it would be done in a planned manner, within an organised military structure; but, probably, they had their own ideas and they were planning. But their planning and the planned design of operations that would be performed by a military structure cannot be compared.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would criminals plan their activities?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same would apply. I guess they planned their own work, but this cannot be compared as planning by a military organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Dr. Markovski --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, you were also asked about the road Skopje-Tetovo, that it was closed. Can you please tell us, according to your knowledge, when was this road closed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it well. The road was closed as an intervention by the Ministry of Interior, that is to say, the police, because immediately after the incident, there was a crime scene inspection team, which was also joined by the chief public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Dzikov. That is why during the on-site investigation or investigation for two or three hours, I don't recall, the road was closed by just a single lane.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: During any other period in 2001, do you remember if the road was closed at all?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It wasn't closed in any other event during the crisis, for the reasons that we are discussing now, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you also if there is a serious traffic accident, in order to conduct a crime scene investigation, would you close the road?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a personal experience, and people have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the on-site investigation is completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Regarding Karpalak, one more question: Can you please tell us what was the transport vehicle used in order to transport the soldiers that were under attack?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I give the answer, I have to apologise. Because when we were discussing this with the Prosecutor, I mentioned a bus and actually I should have said a truck. I do apologise for this lack of precision. So they were being transported both with a bus, but also trucks have been used.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me go back to Radusa. Was there a written order for the action in Radusa, ordered by the president?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, there wasn't. The president did not issue an order because, basically, we are discussing defensive activities by the police. The police was challenged, and that is why it undertook defensive measures and activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the expert please be shown P00604, page 2. Could we see the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember that my learned colleague from the Prosecution showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the second page of the English version as well. The second page in the English version, please. I'm going to read it in Macedonian. It says here that: "According to the information of UBK, Dzemal Huseini, one of the UBK commanders ..." Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you: Do you know who this person is, from your personal information, of course?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Does the name Jamie Shane ring any bells to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have heard that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the recent action of the Ministry of Interior Affairs forces. It was an action of two months ago, and this person organised a group of armed extremists in the area of the village of Brodec and actually found shelter in the village of Brodec, in Tetovo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not understand how events that occurred in the Republic of Macedonia two months ago are relevant to the matters at the heart of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was my last question, because it is our position that the 2001 was not a year of isolated terrorist events, but it is something that is happening in the Republic of Macedonia even now and happened even before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we must say to you, Mr. Apostolski, that is not your last question. Your last question was the previous one. This one won't be pursued.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm grateful, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness -- for the expert, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Apostolski. You will be pleased to know, sir, that that completes the questioning for you. We are grateful that you have come to The Hague and for the time that you have been able to give in this matter. You are now, of course, able to return to your normal activities. Is there any matter that needs to be raised at this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please address this Chamber, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very briefly, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the end, I would like to express my respect to the Honorable Chamber, and I would like to express my respect to Mr. Saxon and Mr. Bezruchenko and to the people on the left side of me, and I would like to say my thanks to all the services of this Court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If there is no special matter we now adjourn until next Tuesday, when we expect to hear the last evidence, and that I believe is Tuesday afternoon at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of March, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.35 p.m.,
